\title{\textbf{NS-SBM}\\[4pt]
  \large A Course in Incompressible Navier--Stokes on an\\
  Immersed-Boundary GPU Solver\\[2pt]
  \normalsize Monolithic VMS \; $\cdot$ \; Pressure Projection \; $\cdot$ \; Nitsche \; $\cdot$ \; SBM}
\author{DiffSim project}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\noindent This course teaches the simulation of \emph{incompressible
Navier--Stokes flow} on DiffSim's GPU-native, equal-order ($P_1/P_1$)
residual-based-VMS solver. It is built around two production engines: the
\textbf{monolithic VMS saddle solver} --- the correctness \emph{oracle} ---
and the \textbf{pressure-projection (Helmholtz--Leray) solver} --- the
\emph{scalable} engine whose symmetric-positive-definite pressure step is
the path to hundred-million-DOF simulations. Along the way it teaches weak
imposition of Dirichlet conditions (\textbf{Nitsche's method}) and the
\textbf{Shifted Boundary Method} (SBM), which lets an immersed body sit
\emph{off} the mesh grid. Every concept pairs a written derivation --- read
from the code, with \texttt{file:line} citations --- with a runnable module;
you reproduce the drag and centerline numbers here, then explore the knobs
on your own. Every ``expected result'' number was produced by running the
module on the GPU box, not invented.
\end{abstract}

\tableofcontents

\chapter{Using this course}
Read a concept below, then open its module folder
(\file{tutorials/ns-sbm-course/<NN\_name>/}), run \file{run.py}, and
compare your printed self-check table and figures with the ones in this
document. The modules call the same production steppers
(\file{diffsim.steppers.*}) and SBM code (\file{diffsim.sbm.*}) the
research code uses --- there are no toy re-implementations.

The spine of the course is a single comparison, repeated at rising
complexity: \emph{does the scalable pressure-projection split reproduce
the same-mesh monolithic oracle?} Chapters 1--2 establish the two engines
on a closed cavity; Chapter 3 adds an immersed body with weak (Nitsche)
no-slip at $d=0$; Chapter 4 turns on a genuine sub-cell SBM shift
($d\neq0$); Chapter 5 goes to 3-D. Chapters 6--8 are the forward-looking
placeholders (scaling to 100M DOF, multi-GPU, and differentiable
structure).

Boxes flag the two things you act on:
\begin{keybox}\textbf{Key idea.} The load-bearing concept.\end{keybox}
\begin{runbox}\textbf{Run it.} The command, and what to compare.\end{runbox}
Questions marked \textbf{\textcolor{purple!70!black}{Q}} are for you to
explore --- they have no answers printed here on purpose.
